en: The Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Sovereign King Sūtra,
Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India during the Tang Dynasty, by Imperial Decree.

Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāmitābhāya tathāgatāya. Namo ’ryavairocanāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Tadyathā | oṃ amogha-pratihatā hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the aforementioned Sovereign King of Mantras, the Amogha-dhāraṇī.
This is the sovereign of all secret mantras.
If there is anyone who can recite this mantra and achieve its accomplishment,
they will immediately attain mastery over all mantras.
However, all activities pertaining to the dhāraṇī method shall be brought to fulfillment.
Chapter One: The Exposition by the Venerable One on the Merits of the Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Furthermore, the method for the King of Divine Mantras, Amoghapāśa, is taught:
if one achieves it, the merit shall not be in vain,
and it will enable the realms of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings [to attain liberation].
All karmic obstructions will be completely purified;
one will be able to accumulate immeasurable provisions of merit and increase the roots of goodness through skillful means.
They will penetrate the boundless realm of wisdom;
the six pāramitās will all be brought to perfection;
and they will further be able to realize unsurpassed bodhi.
The four fearlessnesses, the eighteen unique qualities, and all the Buddha-dharmas;
as well as the four noble truths, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment;
furthermore, they are able to manifest the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), various samādhis, and samāpattis.
Furthermore, they are able to realize the stages of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and tathāgata;
they achieve wisdom, intelligence, and sharp faculties,
and possess great majestic power and the strength of diligence.
Endowed with eloquence, he ascended into the air and vanished from sight.
For the sake of King Karkarava-raiti, who possesses all sovereign power,
he was able to become a mantra-seer and bring peace and happiness to the world.
One obtains the auspicious vase and the wish-fulfilling jewel;
whatever is to be done accordingly is all accomplished.
One can command the messengers, and their advancing or retreating will never be in defiance.
It causes the rākṣasas to act according to one's will;
furthermore, it enables one to enter the cave of the asuras,
or to burn various incenses, or to place medicinal substances in the eyes.
One will be able to see all hidden treasures beneath the earth;
whatever undertakings one performs will be spontaneously accomplished;
one will cure various illnesses, subdue spirits and deities, and protect the ritual mandala.
They cause all the dragon kings to rejoice and be glad;
they attain mastery over both sending down rain and stopping it,
and furthermore, they attain mastery among all human beings.
It can cause all sins, calamities, and hardships to be completely extinguished;
whatever wealth, resources, or treasures one seeks shall be obtained.
Furthermore, it enables the accomplishment of boundless dharani-gates and samadhi-gates.
This dharma of the Great Amoghapāśa Divine Mantra is the most supreme, excellent, and vast among all mantras;
it is capable of [subduing] all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
All bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, rākṣasas,
nakṣatras, vighnas, and so forth.
They shall be served, honored, respected, and praised;
furthermore, they shall be protected by Śakra and the various Brahmā kings,
and they shall be collectively celebrated and comforted by all the siddha-mantra practitioners.
Furthermore, it is that which is practiced by those who are eternally free from all distraction and attachment;
they receive, uphold, and make offerings to what has been taught, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it.
Chapter Two: The Section on the Method for Accomplishing, Maintaining, and Making Offerings to the Divine Mantra. At that time, the Holy Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Furthermore, the method for reciting divine mantras is explained:
if one wishes to recite this divine mantra,
one should first bathe and don fresh, clean garments.
Purify yourself, recite mantras, and receive the bodhisattva precepts.
Generate a mind of compassion and a resolute intention of pity for all sentient beings.
Speak words of truth and remain far removed from envy.
They bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings;
with a straightforward mind and pure faith,
they delight in meritorious qualities and abandon greed, hatred, and delusion.
Mindfully recollecting the Triple Gem and vowing to repay its kindness,
one should extensively make offerings to the Holy Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with incense,
flowers, unguents, and powdered incense.
Adorning it with banners, streamers, and various flower canopies,
one should, before the Venerable One, with single-minded pure faith and firm resolve,
recite the Noble Amoghapāśa Heart Mantra King one hundred and eight times.
He immediately enters the samādhi-gate of the Amogha-dhāraṇī,
forms the lotus mudrā, restrains his inhalation and exhalation, and remains in silence.
By means of this, all that this person ought to accomplish shall be fully attained.
Thereupon, within the dream, one shall behold the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
appearing either in the form of a bhikṣu, or in the form of a brāhmaṇa, or in the form of a youth.
Sometimes manifesting in the form of a sovereign or sometimes in the form of a minister, they address the one reciting the mantra, saying:
"Excellent, O noble man! You are able to receive and uphold that which I have spoken."
"May all that you love and delight in be fully accomplished.
What do you now desire from holding this mantra?
Seek whatever you wish according to your inclination, and I shall cause your vow to be swiftly fulfilled."
By this, one attains the extinction of all karmic obstructions;
one shall never again fall into the realms of hell or animals,
but shall always be born among all the auspicious destinies.
With prajñā manifest before them, their eloquence is unimpeded, and their right mindfulness increases.
Devas follow them in accord as companions;
they act with mastery and without obstruction, endowed with great majestic power.
Furthermore, one will be able to maintain the dhāraṇī according to one's heart's desire;
one shall not be plundered by any enemies or thieves,
and shall be praised by the worthy and holy ones.
He is always respected by kings, ministers, brahmins, householders, and others;
he is beloved by all sentient beings, who offer him sustenance,
pay him homage, serve him, prostrate before him, and praise him with virtuous words.
He constantly serves as a refuge for all who are terrified and is able to win the hearts and minds of all virtuous people.
If there be anyone who constantly recites this divine mantra, [they shall likewise attain these qualities].
All obstacles arising from the three types of unwholesome karma will be completely extinguished.
If one recites it ten thousand times,
there shall be no lack of food, drink, bedding, medicinal decoctions, clothing, or household utensils as required.
Peace, happiness, freedom from illness, long life, and mastery.

Part Three: The Method for Accomplishing the Direct Vision of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. If there is a person who wishes to obtain the direct vision of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
One should go to a quiet mountain monastery, a stupa, or a temple;
or to a grove, a riverbank, a deep mountain, a rocky valley, or an araṇya hermitage.
There, wearing fresh and clean robes and observing the eightfold fast, one should dwell.
Having received the bodhisattva precepts, one’s three karmas are purified;
entering samādhi, one cultivates the four brahma-vihāras without any sense of stinginess,
and constantly seeks joy in the presence of those who maintain the precepts and possess merit.
Thereafter, having received the dharma of the mantra before the image of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
and once the dharma has been received, one should immediately sit in the full lotus posture upon *śarīra* grass in that pure place.
One should recite the Heart Mantra of Amoghapāśa with single-minded concentration and without wavering.
Whether by day or by night, one shall feel neither alarm nor fear,
even if suddenly hearing [sounds] from within the void.
Even upon hearing the sound of a tiger’s roar, they shall not be startled or terrified.
If they see or hear the music, song, dance, and performances of the various devas in the sky, they should not be alarmed or find it strange.
Or they may see the heavens raining *māndārava* flowers and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.
They were not startled or amazed even by *padma*, *utpala*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers.
At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara—
Approaching that person, he proclaimed, "Excellent, excellent!
Since you are able to make such offerings to me,
what do you seek by reciting and upholding this divine mantra?"
The person reciting the mantra immediately rose from their seat,
burned incense and scattered flowers before the Venerable One,
and mixed water with non-glutinous rice and various kinds of flowers.
He made offerings to the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
circumambulated him three times to the right, and prostrated with his head at the Bodhisattva’s feet.
At that time, the Bodhisattva granted him everything according to his wishes.

4. The Section on the Method for Accomplishing the Painting and the Scroll. This is the fourth section, the method for accomplishing the painting and the scroll. At that time, the Venerable One explained the ritual for painting the image as well as the methods for accomplishing mantras.
When painting an image of the holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, one should weave the silk or cotton cloth according to its required length and width without cutting both ends.
The pigments used should be mixed with fragrant glue; do not take any other kind of glue.
The painter must first receive the eightfold precepts of the fast;
only then may he paint the image of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
His body is yellowish-white, his head wears a flower crown, and his dark blue hair falls over both shoulders in front and back.
His compassionate countenance was serene and joyful, emitting hundreds of thousands of rays of light;
his pure and sublime face had three eyes,
and his shoulders and chest were draped with a cord of pure white thread.
He covered his shoulders with the skin of a kṛṣṇamṛga deer king,
adorned his waist with a jeweled belt,
and possessed four arms.
The upper left hand holds a lotus,
and the lower left hand holds a water flask (kamaṇḍalu).
The upper right hand bestows fearlessness (abhaya-mudrā), and the lower right hand holds a rosary (akṣamālā).
All were adorned with rare jewels;
they wore celestial garments and stood upon lotus flowers,
possessing great majesty and virtue, and arrayed in necklaces both short and long.
The crossed shoulders hang down, adorned with ear-rings,
armlets, and bracelets, all decorated with precious jewels.
Upon the crown of the head, Amitāyus Buddha is depicted.
Within the frame, various flowers are to be painted.
If one wishes to construct a maṇḍala during the spring or autumn,
it should be done on the eighth or fifteenth day of the bright fortnight.
When the auspicious stars are favorable and it is a chosen time free from wind and clouds,
one should select a suitable location outside the city according to the specific directions and terrain,
where there are trees with roots, trunks, branches, and leaves.
Flowers and fruits were lush and abundant, with branches and vines entwined together.
Everywhere there were flowing springs and bathing pools,
and verdant green grasses covered the ground in every place.
One should apply yellow earth as mud to coat the ground,
performing all kinds of repairs so that everything conforms to the Dharma;
one must not [perform these acts] on wretched ground consisting of thorns, rubble, bones, stones, or the like.
The four sides of the altar are made with refined gold, red earth, realgar, lime, and purple-gold;
they are marked with boundary lines in blue, yellow, red, white, and purple.
On each side of the altar, a gate is opened.
Outside each gate there are two auspicious pillars (*śalākā*).
Within the mandala, one should draw the conch-shaped *svastika* and the incense seal (*gandhamudrā*).
Inside each gate there are two auspicious vases (*kalaśa*).
In whatever location it is appropriate, one should construct a bathing pool.
Within the pool, it should be filled everywhere with *utpala* flowers, *kumuda* flowers, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers.
On the four sides of the pool, one should paint the forms of geese.
Like a garland of flowers strung together and encircling it on all sides,
one should place the painted image within the mandala;
then scatter various kinds of flowers and burn various kinds of incense.
One should make offerings of banners, pennants, and precious canopies.
Alternatively, one may fashion auspicious vases (*maṅgalakalaśa*) out of gold, silver, various jewels, or red copper;
these should be filled to the brim with all kinds of exquisite fragrant medicines, *maṇi* gems, pearls, gold, silver, and other such treasures, mixed together.
Tie a cord of various flowers around the neck of the flask.
Take burnt rice grains to make flowers,
and scatter them as an adornment upon the altar.
One should cover it with a white canopy.
At each of the four corners of the altar, station one person,
clad in armor and bearing weapons, to guard it.
At that time, the mantra-practitioner bathes and purifies himself three times each day,
puts on fresh and clean garments,
and maintains the precepts with the three karmas purified.
Before the image of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
one should make offerings by filling vessels with milk-rice, ghee, curd, granulated sugar, and rock honey.
Thereafter, one should offer worship by burning blended incenses such as candana, agallochum, storax,
and camphor before the painted image.
Having spread auspicious kusha grass and assumed the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*),
one forms the lotus mudrā with hands placed at the heart in *añjali* and pays homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Then recite the mantra for protecting the body.
The second mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amogha-pratihatā rakṣa rakṣa [insert one's own name] hūṃ phaṭ. When wishing to protect the body, take a single strand of one's own hair.
One should recite this mantra twenty-one times;
it will constantly protect one's own person so that no one can cause harm.
Mantra:
The third mantra for subjugating spirits and deities is as follows:
Oṃ amogha-maṇḍa hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. If one wishes to subjugate spirits and deities, one should first recite this mantra.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over five-colored threads and tie them on the four sides of the altar.
Then, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over water,
or over mustard seeds, or over purified ashes.
Scatter [the substances] within the mandala toward the four directions;
this will immediately cause all evil spirits and ghosts to be unable to cause disturbance or confusion.
This is the fourth incantation for restraining evil spirits, which says:
Oṃ amoghapratiṣṭhā oṃ hūṃ phaṭ. If one intends to restrain evil spirits, one should recite this mantra.
One should empower water by reciting it one hundred and eight times.
Alternatively, one may consecrate white mustard seeds or pure ashes with mantras and scatter them outside the altar in the four directions,
so that malevolent spirits may find no opportunity to cause harm.
The fifth mantra for subduing evil māras is as follows:
Oṃ amogha tiśalocaye vijaya kuru maḥ phaṭ. When casting spells upon a māra, one should recite this mantra.
Recite the mantra over water one hundred and eight times,
or over white mustard seeds and consecrated ashes,
and scatter them in the ten directions outside the mandala.
Immediately, all evil māras will be restrained and unable to cause disturbance.
This is the sixth mantra for restraining the mantras and incantations of evil māras, which is recited as follows:
Oṃ amogha-rakṣa [insert one’s own name] svāhā. When one wishes to restrain the mantras and incantations of evil māras, [one should recite this].
One should recite this mantra over water one hundred and eight times,
or over white mustard seeds and consecrated ashes. Then,
one should apply [the substances] to the crown of the head, the forehead, the heart, and the two shoulders.
Sprinkle it over their bodies;
this will immediately cause all evil spirits and malevolent demons to be unable to disturb or harass them.
This is the seventh mantra for reciting over one's companions.
Oṃ amogha hūṃ kha. If one wishes to empower a companion,
one should recite this mantra and consecrate water one hundred and eight times.
Alternatively, one may scatter white mustard seeds and consecrated ashes within the maṇḍala and sprinkle them upon one's companions;
this will immediately protect those persons.
No evil spirits or demons will be able to cause disturbance or confusion.
The eighth mantra for incantation over incense is as follows:
Oṃ amogha dama dama hūṃ phaṭ. When burning incense, [recite this].
First, use this mantra to consecrate various kinds of incense twenty-one times;
thereafter, burn the incense and make offerings with reverence.
The ninth mantra for consecrating food, drink, flowers, and fruits is as follows:
Oṃ amogha-kṣa-hrīṇe kṣa-hrīṇe hūṃ phaṭ. When one wishes to scatter food, drink, flowers, fruits, and so forth, [one should recite this].
First, recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
Then, outside the mandala,
scatter it everywhere, following the four directions.
The tenth mantra for accomplishing whatever task one undertakes is as follows:
Oṃ amogha-vijaya hūṃ phaṭ. Whatever task one performs, if this mantra is recited, it shall be accomplished entirely.
O World-Honored One, the mantra-holder,
having performed this rite,
[should do so] within the mandala.
One should recite the Sovereign King of Amogha Dhāraṇīs.
If the painted image of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva moves,
or if smoke issues forth, or if flames issue forth.
As when reciting mantras as usual, one should not be alarmed or terrified.
If one sees the painted image move, one will obtain wealth, nobility, and mastery.
If one sees smoke emerge, one will achieve the rank of a cakravartin king.
If one sees flames rising and surging into the air, one will attain mastery as a mantra-adept (vidyādhara).
As for the reciter of the mantra, if they see the flames emerge,
their mind shall be free from alarm and fear, and their body shall remain unshaken.
Immediately, the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will manifest before that person and comfort them;
having seen him, all that the person seeks shall be fulfilled.
They immediately attain the various samādhis of a bodhisattva,
achieve non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and,
in their present bodies, remember the events of their past lives.
And one shall obtain immeasurable hundreds of thousands of merits.
5. The Section on the Accomplishment of the Duties of the Messenger (Dūta-karmasādhana-vibhāga), Part Five. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
Furthermore, it is taught that the messenger is capable of accomplishing the ritual procedures.
This messenger is none other than the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
the messenger of the *Amoghapāśa-rāja-mantra*.
If one wishes to command them,
one should use colored pigments and cotton cloth to paint the form of the messenger upon a scroll, depicting him as a yakṣa youth.
His hair stands erect like a blazing flame;
his face is wrathful with green eyes and a flat nose;
his complexion is red and he wears red garments.
From his mouth emerge four fangs, two above and two below;
his tongue enters and exits from his mouth.
In one hand he holds a sword, and in the other he grasps a lasso.
All the requisites for adorning the body are fully prepared.
When one wishes to perform the rite,
on the eighth or fourteenth day of the waxing moon, one should observe the fast and maintain purity.
One should place the painted image at a crossroads or within an empty room,
and should offer various kinds of worship with flowers, incense,
and food and drink, excluding meat, blood, and the like.
The mantra-holder should first recite the mantra to protect his own body.
Before the cotton-painted image, he should recite the Amogharāja-mantra one hundred and eight times.
At that time, the messenger will appear before that person.
He said to the mantra-holders, "What do you require?
Whatever you command, I shall accomplish.
Then, according to the desires of those mantra-holders, the messengers carried out their instructions.
At that time, the messenger shall recount everything he has seen and heard in full detail.
If the mantra-practitioner requests one hundred gold coins daily, they shall be obtained immediately.
However, these must not be used for other purposes, nor should any stinginess arise regarding them.
One should merely make offerings to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.
Such matters as these should be known only by oneself;
one must not speak of them to others indiscriminately.
Furthermore, one must not harbor resentment toward others.
One should consume pure food and must not eat impure food.
At every mealtime, one should first set aside a portion of one's own food and drink.
One should offer food to the messengers first and then eat oneself.
One must always maintain mindfulness and not forget this.
With a mind constantly free from greed, hatred, and delusion, one must not speak falsely.
He utters words of truth and preaches the Dharma for others;
he constantly gives rise to a mind of benefit, compassion, and loving-kindness toward all sentient beings.
Furthermore, with incense, flowers, robes, banners, pennants, and precious canopies, he makes offerings.
With a mind of gratitude, one should constantly make offerings of unguents, powdered incense, burning incense, and scattered flowers to the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
If one can do so, the messengers will attend upon and serve them day after day.
He obtained all the necessary provisions required by the five hundred people:
food, drink, clothing, ointments, powdered incense,
burning incense, and scattered flowers were all fully provided.
Furthermore, for as long as one maintains this dhāraṇī until the end of one's life,
all that is desired shall be obtained without any deficiency.
*The Sovereign King Dhāraṇī of the Amoghapāśa*, Scroll One.
The Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Sovereign King Sūtra, Scroll II,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of India, Prajñā, during the Tang Dynasty, by Imperial Decree.

6. The Section on the Accomplishment of the Subjugation of Servants and Messengers. This is the sixth section, on the accomplishment of the subjugation of servants and messengers. At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara again spoke these words:
If one wishes to achieve the subjugation of servants,
the mantra-holder should first fashion the form of a servant;
this messenger is indeed the servant of the *Amoghapāśa-rāja* dhāraṇī.
With a handsome and upright countenance,
one should adorn their body with every kind of ornament.
One should fashion five topknots upon his head;
his physical appearance should be like that of a youth.
When performing this, one should use white sandalwood.
Alternatively, one may use red sandalwood or exquisite agarwood;
or use celestial wood or any kind of wood;
or fashion its form from gold or silver.
When painting the scroll, whether on white cotton cloth or silk,
all the garments of the servants should be made red,
using lac mixed with the juice of purple mineral (manjiṣṭhā).
Furthermore, using vermilion and saffron— whether from the root or the fragrant powder—
one should paint its form with various colors,
making it dignified and beautiful, with a joyful and serene countenance, smiling gently.
His physical form and appearance are pale yellowish-white;
he should be depicted with two arms,
one hand holding an *āmra* fruit.
Holding various flowers in one hand,
this image should always be installed in a secluded place.
One should scatter flowers, burn incense, use powdered incense, apply unguents, and light lamps.
One should make offerings of various kinds of food and drink.
Furthermore, before the image, one should recite the Amoghapāśarāja-dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times.
The practitioner of the mantra should observe the eight precepts and give rise to a mind of compassion.
The mantra-rite will be accomplished immediately;
one will then be able to behold the form of that messenger and command them with complete mastery.
Whatever this mantra-holder commands shall all be accomplished;
furthermore, whether by what the messenger hears with their ears or sees with their eyes, they shall come and report it all to the mantra-holder.
It enables the mantra-holder to travel swiftly to and from wherever they may be directed;
all undertakings shall be successfully accomplished,
and it can further bestow upon the mantra-holder all manner of wealth and treasures.
According to wherever the practitioner of the mantra desires to go,
that messenger shall immediately take them there;
and wherever the practitioner of the mantra dwells, the messenger shall likewise bring them back.
If one constantly sweeps and sprinkles the ground as if applying mud,
all secret matters as well as auspicious events will come to be told to them.
All evil sounds and all sufferings shall be completely extinguished;
all illnesses shall be healed and cured;
and all malevolent spirits and ghosts shall naturally vanish and disappear.
All poisons are dissolved and dispersed, joy is perfected,
all meritorious deeds increase,
and all sinful acts are entirely extinguished.
Just as a filial son reverently makes offerings to his father,
so too should that mantra-holder, if he desires peace and happiness for himself,
not [behave] toward that messenger.
If one has committed acts of slighting or deception, harbored malice, or felt anger,
one should bathe for purification and constantly and diligently recite mantras while practicing offerings, refraining from false speech.
With a heart of compassion for all sentient beings, he bestows fearlessness upon them;
he gives rise to profound and pure faith in the Triple Gem,
and constantly scatters various flowers, hangs flower garlands, and burns incense and powdered incense.
With these and other such offerings,
one should worship the Venerable Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, one should first worship the messengers with various foods and drinks, scattered flowers, burned incense, and lit lamps.
One must not, even for a single day, forget to make offerings.
If one does not make offerings, the sought-after objective will not be accomplished;
the messenger will vanish from sight and immediately depart.
Therefore, those who uphold mantras should not be negligent;
they should always cultivate diligence and never be indolent.
They should always diligently make offerings at places of reverence.
One should never forget or lose the bodhicitta.
Regarding generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom,
one should constantly practice them while remaining far removed from stinginess, the defilement of violating precepts, and all dust-like impurities.
They constantly give rise to fear within the cycle of birth and death;
they harbor deep shame and remorse, maintain constant right mindfulness,
and do not allow their wisdom to become distracted, observing with discernment.
If one acts in this manner, one will be able to accomplish all mantra-activities.
Section Seven: The Method for Accomplishing the Auspicious Vase. At that time, the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
Furthermore, the method for accomplishing the auspicious vase (*śrīkumbha*) is explained.
If a mantra-practitioner wishes to accomplish this rite,
they should form a companion group and cultivate the ten wholesome actions with firm and sincere resolve.
When one wishes to construct a maṇḍala, one should select an auspicious location.
It may be a mountain forest, a site of good fortune,
or a secluded place where sages of old once dwelt.
Having bathed and purified himself according to the Dharma,
he dressed in new garments, ate only barley and milk gruel,
and observed the eightfold precepts of the fast.
Together with one's companions, recite mantras to protect oneself.
According to one's preference for distance, construct a square mandala with a gate on each side;
smear the ground with fragrant mud and draw lotus petals with incense.
One should demarcate the path with powders of realgar, red earth, and *candana* (sandalwood).
Within that mandala, one should paint the four great heavenly kings according to the four directions.
Their bodies are adorned with various precious objects;
all are clad in armor and weapons, holding swords and blades in their hands.
On the eastern side of the maṇḍala, one should paint Vajrapāṇi.
Swords are depicted on the southern side;
clubs are painted on the western side;
and spears are painted on the northern side.
At its four corners, draw red banners and scatter various kinds of flowers.
In the center of the mandala, paint auspicious vases using various colors.
Tie a garland of various flowers around the neck of the flask.
Fill the flask to the brim with water from a lotus pond.
Furthermore, place fragrant flowers, wonderful medicines, various fruits, and all kinds of seeds [inside].
Furthermore, gold, silver, pearls, and other such jewels were all placed inside the vases.
Additionally, four platters were used;
on one platter, curd was set out.
One tray was filled with ghee,
one tray was filled with milk,
and one tray was filled with honey.

At that time, the mantra-practitioner subdued that nāga and exhorted him to establish a vow to constantly benefit all sentient beings;
he then further conferred the precepts upon him.
By the power of these roots of goodness,
that nāga cast off his animal body and attained the stage of non-retrogression,
eventually realizing unsurpassed bodhi.
Because this mantra-practitioner bestows their very life for the benefit of sentient beings,
their *dānapāramitā* (perfection of giving) becomes fully perfected;
they shall not be reborn within the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals.
One shall constantly be reborn among humans and devas and swiftly attain the stage of Buddhahood.

Chapter Fifteen: The Section on Accomplishing the Vision of the King of the Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī. If there are those who wish to obtain the vision of the King of the Amoghapāśa Divine Spell, [they should proceed as follows].
The mantra-practitioner should first bathe,
don fresh and clean garments, and strictly observe the prohibitions and precepts;
thereafter, they should select a secluded place.
Whether beneath a tree, beside a stūpa, or within a grove,
on the eighth or fourteenth day of the bright fortnight,
one should prepare the ground to form a maṇḍala and sprinkle it with water.
Having spread auspicious grass (kuśa), one should recite this mantra.
One should bind one's topknot and protect one's body.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ āmukapratistha rakṣa rakṣa [name] hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Having recited this mantra:
One should recite the mantra of the Amoghapāśarāja three times over white mustard seeds and scatter them in the four directions;
immediately all obstructing spirits and deities [will be subdued].
They retreated and fled, unable to cause any disturbance.
Thereafter, he sat cross-legged upon the grass,
covered his head with his robe, and assumed the mudrā of meditative concentration.
One should recite the King of Mantras of the Amoghapāśa one thousand and eight times.
At that time, there will immediately be a great sound and a great radiance, or flowers will descend from the sky.
One who maintains the mantra, upon seeing or hearing such things, should not be alarmed or terrified.
One should know that this is the accomplishment of the rite for beholding the Venerable Amoghapāśarāja.
Thereafter, one should rise from one's seat, burn incense, and scatter flowers.
With single-minded recollection, the Venerable Noble Avalokiteśvara surveyed the ten directions and immediately beheld the Noble Amoghapāśa King of Divine Mantras approaching from the south,
traveling through the air.
His majestic radiance blazes like hundreds of thousands of lightning bolts.
His body is adorned with all manner of precious jewels.
He has three eyes on his face and manifests a wrathful expression.
From his mouth and teeth, hair emerges like flames;
its color is dark and billowing, resembling summer clouds.
His body has four arms.
In one hand he holds a sword,
and in the other hand he holds a lasso;
the sword and lasso he wields are ablaze with flames.
Clad in red garments, the breath from his nostrils issued forth like a blazing flame,
filling the entirety of space with brilliant radiance.
All his hands and feet were adorned with genuine gold, vajra-maṇis, and vaidūrya.
With great dragon kings serving as his necklaces,
he let out a loud laugh like the sound of a celestial drum; his form was terrifying,
causing mountains and rivers to surge and trees to break.
Although the mantra-holder may see such various extraordinary signs,
they should not be terrified;
they should simply recite the King of Mantras, the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa.
Then, with single-minded recollection, one should offer incense and scatter flowers to the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, one should offer pure water mixed with white non-glutinous rice as an offering.
At that time, the King of Mantras will descend from the sky, his appearance serene and tranquil.
Just as a celestial being with a joyful and smiling countenance, he praised the mantra-reciter, saying, "Excellent, excellent!
I am now delighted; what do you seek?"
If one seeks sovereign peace and happiness,
or the status of a *rāja*, one performs the *kṣāravati-rāja-vidhi*.
Whether it be for invisibility, soaring through the air, or becoming a *vidyādhara*— a *vidyādhara-kṣāravati-rāja*.
Whether it be Śakra, or Brahmā, or the World Protectors;
whether it be the knowledge of recollecting past lives, or the five supernormal powers;
or the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, or the fruit of pratyekabuddhahood.
Up to the path of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
follow whatever you desire;
as for that which you desire, perform prostrations and seek it.
One should speak as stated above:
"You may act as my messenger.
At that time, the mantra-deity shall act as the messenger.
They will carry out every instruction given to them;
they will constantly follow wherever one goes,
and they will report everything seen and heard back to the person who recites the mantra.
If the mantra-practitioner does not approach and dwell near the King of Mantras,
it will depart of its own accord;
yet when the practitioner calls it to mind, it will arrive immediately at the appropriate time.
Alternatively, one may bestow hidden treasures upon the mantra-practitioner,
or reveal such treasures to them;
or, if the mantra-practitioner sees a person afflicted by demonic illness and desires to treat them.
The messenger shall immediately dispel them and punish them;
he can cause diseases such as chills and fevers to be extinguished,
and can also restrain all water, fire, swords, poison, clouds, dragons, and bandits.
Furthermore, it can crush the armies and enemies of others;
it never fails to comply with whatever the mantra-holder commands.
Even when the practitioner is angry, [the spirit] dares not be angry in return nor does it flee.
If the mantra-practitioner acts contrary to the Dharma or is timid and weak, there will be no accomplishment.
Therefore, the practitioner should always act in accordance with the Dharma and diligently cultivate meritorious deeds;
thus, without requiring excessive effort, they shall attain accomplishment.
16. Chapter Sixteen: The Section on Accomplishing the Vision of the Tathāgata’s Dharma.
If there are those who wish to behold the Tathāgata, that mantra-practitioner should perform the ten wholesome actions.
Arousing a heart of compassion and generating the superior intention (*adhyāśaya*),
one should cultivate firm diligence and make a solemn vow,
desiring to benefit all sentient beings.
Make offerings to the Triple Gem.
Before an image of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
smear the ground and construct an altar.
One should provide various requisites as far as one's means allow,
such as lamps, candles, flowers, and incense, to perform offerings;
having purified one's body, one should wear fresh white garments.
Bathe and change one's clothes three times each day.
Within the mandala, observe a fast for either three days or seven days,
sitting in the full lotus posture and forming the seal of the Tathāgata.
One should recite the King of Mantras of the Heart of Amoghapāśa.
At that time, the image of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will tremble or manifest miraculous transformations.
Whether walking or sitting, whether lowering or raising [the body],
whether manifesting as one body or many bodies, whether coarse or subtle,
or rising into the air and emitting great radiance.
If one sees such various extraordinary signs,
one should know that this is the accomplishment of the mantra method.
The practitioner of the mantra should cause Samantabhadra to behold the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, by means of these signs, the Noble Avalokiteśvara caused Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to entreat the World-Honored One so that the person reciting the mantra might see him.
Furthermore, by this it should be understood that the Tathāgata granted the request made by the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
out of a desire to benefit and have compassion for all sentient beings.
At that time, the mantra-holder, seeing such signs, rejoiced and leaped for joy.
He then further offered various kinds of ritual implements as offerings to the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
One should recite the King of Mantras, the Heart of Amoghapāśa, up until the point where the image of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appears upon its seat and then vanishes. Thereupon,
the Tathāgata appears and extends his golden arm.
The consoling mantra practitioner utters these words: "O you,
because the Tathāgata, the Greatly Compassionate One, takes pity upon you,
I shall fulfill whatever aspirations you desire."
At that time, the mantra-practitioner gazed up at the World-Honored One;
leaping for joy and filled with delight, he circumambulated him seven times to the right.
Having completed his offerings of incense and flowers and his acts of veneration, he finished.
He addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One, I now see the Tathāgata with my physical eyes.
May whatever I aspire for be fulfilled."
At that time, the World-Honored One said to the mantra-practitioner:
"I shall grant you everything according to your wishes.
What do you seek now?"
Whether seeking extensive learning,
or seeking wealth, treasures, prosperity, and sovereignty,
or seeking the state of a mantra-adept (vidyādhara).
If, within the Dharma of the Tathāgata,
one seeks the enlightenment of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha,
or seeks the rank of an anointed bodhisattva.
If one seeks to be free from illness and to enjoy long life among human beings;
or if one seeks birth in the family of a brahmin householder or a great clan of laypeople;
or in the preeminent birthplace of a wheel-turning king (cakravartin) family.
If one seeks rebirth among the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven,
the Brahmakāyika Heaven, or the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens; or if one seeks the fruits of sainthood.
In such places as these, everything sought shall be obtained,
by virtue of the Tathāgata’s supernormal power, the empowerment of his merit,
and the Tathāgata’s secret mantra.
By the power of the vows of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
by the majestic power of the King of Heart-Mantras, Amoghapāśa;
and because the mental disposition of the mantra-holder is pure.
Because the speech of the Tathāgata is free from falsehood or error,
whatever one aspires for shall certainly be accomplished.
If a mantra-practitioner desires to receive a prophecy (vyākaraṇa) in the presence of the Tathāgata, [they should proceed as follows].
The Tathāgata has likewise bestowed a prophecy upon them.
Those of dull wit and little wisdom should not engage in such discrimination,
nor should they give rise to doubts such as "the Buddha-knowledge is difficult to accomplish."
It requires immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of asaṃkhyeya kalpas to cultivate hundreds of thousands of karmic practices of pure deeds;
only through skillful means can one finally achieve fulfillment.
Do not give rise to this doubt as to how one can obtain a prediction of enlightenment by practicing and accumulating even a small amount of dhāraṇī methods in a single lifetime. Why is this?
Because of the person who upholds the dhāraṇī.
By practicing the skillful means of prajñā,
and through the powers of faith, diligence, mindfulness, and samādhi,
all things are accomplished by these causes and conditions.
Until they attain Buddhahood,
I shall now comfort and empower these people,
exhorting them to arouse diligence and bestowing upon them the prediction of their future enlightenment.
One shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having caused the person who recites the mantra to receive their prediction (*vyākaraṇa*),
one should practice by following the successive stages of the bodhisattva path.
Having attained mastery over all meditative absorptions and samādhis,
such a masterful bodhisattva draws near to anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Therefore, one who recites this mantra should first seek mastery.
If there are those who have not yet tasted the bliss of bodhi, they should give rise to pure faith;
by virtue of the power of that faith, [they shall attain it].
All undertakings will be swiftly brought to their ultimate fulfillment.
If one lacks faith, then even if they were to exert diligence for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kalpas,
their efforts would be in vain.
They will ultimately fail to attain realization and remain far removed from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The World-Honored One, by means of this, fully understands the inclinations and dispositions of sentient beings.
Therefore, he was granted a prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*).
Because the practitioner thus sought a prediction from the World-Honored One,
the Buddha granted him that prediction.
At that time, once the practitioner of mantras has received the prediction,
they should know with certainty: "I shall become a Buddha,
a teacher of gods and humans, and an unsurpassed field of merit."
Yet I have given rise to this thought:
"My body is inferior, born of impurity, impermanent and subject to decay;
its lifespan is brief, and it is oppressed by arising and ceasing."
Furthermore, for what purpose is this body maintained?
It is for the sake of seeking the indestructible body of a Tathāgata;
thus one makes the vow not to commit unwholesome actions of body, speech, or mind.
Constantly practicing wholesome deeds of body, speech,
and mind, one will surely abandon the bodies of the five destinies;
by diligently practicing austerities, one cultivates the causes for Buddhahood.
By the power of the divine spells of the mantra-holder,
one will certainly realize bodhi;
for it is capable of accumulating inconceivable power of merit.
Because of reciting and upholding the Tathāgata’s dhāraṇī,
and because of cultivating the power of the sublime samādhi,
[this is] thus, from within the Tathāgata’s treasury of mantras.
Having thus spoken this divine mantra,
there are the methods for the Great Seal (mahāmudrā), the ritual for binding the maṇḍala, and the ritual for entering the maṇḍala;
as well as the rituals for averting calamities and for increasing merit.
This is the rite for subduing all obstructing spirits through punishment.
If there are those who have faith, one may tame them by means of mantras;
it can manifest the various supernatural transformations of a Bodhisattva.
It brings about auspiciousness through skillful means,
grants health and long life, extinguishes all afflictions, and causes one to transcend the five deeds of immediate retribution;
furthermore, it can eliminate misfortunes, calamities, and obstacles.
It can eliminate epidemics,
as well as spells that raise corpses, demons of nightmares and enchantments,
along with reanimated ghosts and evil omens.
Furthermore, it can cause poisons, sorcery, and weapons;
red sores, black sores, hemorrhoids, and fistulas;
as well as the *saiṃdhava* spirits, epilepsy spirits, shadow spirits, and child-spirits [to be pacified].
By the power of the mantra, they cannot cause harm; furthermore,
one shall obtain physical strength, wealth, sovereignty, peace, and happiness,
as well as a joyful mind and body, wisdom, intelligence, and mindfulness.
Possessing great majesty and virtue, they are revered by all; furthermore,
they are able to accomplish the provisions of merit and wisdom, increase their roots of goodness,
and possess countenances that are upright, radiant, and lovely.
If there is one who accomplishes the method of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara’s King of Mantras, the Amoghapāśahṛdaya,
they shall immediately obtain such immeasurable merit as this.
Just as with a wish-fulfilling jewel or a kalpavṛkṣa tree, one obtains whatever is sought;
so too with this dharma of divine mantras, even if one were to seek it throughout hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kalpas.
It is already difficult to obtain;
how much more so for sentient beings with meager merit to attain this Dharma?
Even the Dharma itself is difficult to obtain, let alone its accomplishment.
One should know that this mantra is difficult to encounter or hear,
for it is upheld by all Tathāgatas and entered into by all Bodhisattvas.
It is that which all Tathāgatas have collectively accomplished;
it is that which all devas protect and guard;
and it is that which those who recite mantras constantly offer worship to.
This is a great mass of merit;
it is able to bring all sentient beings to fulfillment according to their needs and manifests unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
If there are those who receive and uphold this mantra,
and with various flowers, incense, banners, streamers, and precious canopies,
offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise;
They shall never fall into the various evil realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals;
they will always be born before Amitābha Buddha in the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
where their lifespan shall be immeasurable.
All [this] is through the majestic power and spiritual authority of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.

The twenty-sixth mantra: *Namo ratnatrayāya | namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | oṃ amoghapratiṣṭhita saṃhara saṃhara hūṃ phaṭ.* This is the mantra for gathering and removing [obstacles].
Whenever the rites for binding the altar are completed and one wishes to dismantle and remove them,
one must first recite this mantra and only then perform the removal.
*The Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Sovereign King Sūtra*, Scroll Lower.
